//: xrom_sentineld runtime configuration.
Installed to /system_ext/etc/xrom/sentinel.json by PRODUCT_COPY_FILES.
WHAT MAY AND MAY NOT BE CONFIGURED HERE
Ceilings, thresholds, paths and the list of uids allowed to report a threat.
NOTHING that decides what is trusted: no key material, no trust anchors, no
pinned digests. A configuration file on a writable partition that could relax a
signature check would be a signature check that one file write disables, so the
keys stay compiled into the image.
A missing file is not an error and the daemon runs the shipped defaults, which
are the values below. A file that exists and does not parse stops the daemon:
guessing what a broken configuration meant is how a security policy ends up
looser than intended. Unknown keys are rejected for the same reason.
The defaults here are deliberately the conservative ones. Every value that is
relaxed relative to common practice has a comment saying what the relaxation
costs.
//reporter_uids: 1000 is system, which covers xrom_avfd's client path and any system component
that detects something. Shell (2000) and root (0) are NOT in this list and are
gated separately by allow_shell_reporter / allow_root_reporter, both of which
additionally require a debuggable build. An adb-reachable threat reporter on a
production build is a remote reboot button.

quarantine.//cancel_window_seconds: The window in which a cancellation is honoured. 0 disables it entirely.
//cancel_requires_authentication: Cancelling requires a keyguard-authenticated user AND a one-time token the
sentinel issued with the prompt. Both halves are needed: the uid check alone
would let any system component cancel any quarantine, and the token alone
would let a non-UI process that read the log pretend to be a user.
//allow_cancel_at_critical: FALSE, AND THIS IS THE ONE PLACE THIS FILE DISAGREES WITH THE OBVIOUS
READING OF THE REQUIREMENT. The UI is part of the system under suspicion.
A dialog offering a way to dismiss a security response is a control surface
handed to whatever compromised the device, and at CRITICAL that is exactly
the component least worth trusting. See correction #7 in docs/05.
quarantine.//reboot_threshold: 0 low, 1 medium, 2 high, 3 critical. HIGH and above reboot.

//: Two counters for two failure classes, and X-ROM owns only one of them.
tries_remaining is the bootloader's and counts boots that never reached
userspace; it is read and never written, because it lives in a misc region
the bootloader, recovery and uncrypt share at offsets that are agreed across
AOSP and not configurable. integrity_failures is X-ROM's and counts boots
that reached userspace and then failed the post-boot comparison, which the
platform counter structurally cannot see. See correction #4 in docs/05.
//tries_remaining_floor: 1, NOT 0. At zero the bootloader has already marked the slot unbootable and
is falling back, so waiting for zero means X-ROM never gets to say anything
about a slot that is dying — which is the only window in which the vault is
useful. The loader rejects 0 for this reason.

//pinned_cidrs: WEAK BY CONSTRUCTION, and kept only because it can push a decision toward
the vault and never toward the network. A CIDR check verifies the shape of a
DNS answer, not the identity of the host: whoever controls the resolver can
return any address inside it. It is also brittle, because these ranges belong
to whoever operates the update host and change without notice. The check that
carries the weight is the TLS public-key pin, compiled into the recovery
Leaving this empty is a doubt, not a pass: a build that forgot the pins must
fail toward the vault rather than toward the network.
//max_package_bytes: 500 MiB. Checked against the manifest's declared size BEFORE a byte is
fetched, because fetching is the expensive step and a multi-gigabyte package
on a metered link is a cost paid before discovering it cannot be installed.
0 disables network installs entirely rather than allowing anything.
//skip_dns_range_check: Off. Turning it on is a deliberate, logged weakening: it stops the DNS range
signal from blocking the remote path. It does NOT affect the TLS pin.

//vault_block_device: Read-only to this daemon by SELinux. xrom_ota_installer is the only domain that
ever holds blk_file write on it, and that separation is enforced by a neverallow
rather than by this daemon being careful. See correction #5 in docs/05.
//vault_meta_block_device: A separate 64 KiB partition, and the split is not tidiness. SELinux labels
block devices and cannot distinguish one offset from another, so a record the
sentinel must be able to write cannot live on a partition where only the OTA
installer may write. Sharing one device would force the neverallow to name the
sentinel as an exception and the property the requirement asks for would be
//deep_integrity_on_boot: FALSE, AND IT SHOULD STAY FALSE. Deep hashes every byte of both partitions:
gigabytes of flash I/O on the boot path, duplicating work dm-verity already does
on every read of the running slot. The cheap comparison uses the AVB hashtree
roots, which are 32 bytes each and already authenticated. See correction #9.
//use_netd_firewall_chain: OPEN RISK, NOT A SOLVED MECHANISM. X-ROM builds with CONFIG_BPF_SYSCALL off and
netd on Android 12+ uses eBPF for parts of its own operation, so whether netd is
functional on this kernel is not known and cannot be determined without a device.
This is why all three layers below are attempted and each reports independently,
instead of the first success ending the attempt: a device where netd is broken and
the ioctl layer works must produce a log that says so, or the question never gets
answered. See correction #10 in docs/05 and section 13 of xrom_avf_verify.sh.
//use_interface_down: The layer that works without netd: SIOCSIFFLAGS on an AF_INET socket, needing
CAP_NET_ADMIN and nothing else. Its effect is also observable without a packet
capture, which the firewall chain's is not.
//use_quarantine_property: Setting a property is NOT itself a network cut. It records the quarantine
durably enough for the recovery image and the next boot to see it, and it is the
signal the device tree's init trigger acts on. If that trigger is not
provisioned this layer is decorative, which is why it is one of three and never
//stash_evidence_in_pvm: FALSE, AND THIS IS A CONFLICT IN THE REQUIREMENTS RATHER THAN AN OVERSIGHT.
Moving evidence into a pVM means submitting a task through IXIsolationService,
which means naming a TaskClass. There is no TaskClass for evidence stashing, and
TaskClass is part of the frozen isolation AIDL this project is constrained not to
change. Repurposing a class the payload already serves would mean the evidence
log is processed by code expecting something else entirely, which is worse than
not sending it. Evidence is staged to staging_log_path with mode 0600 and its
SHA-256 recorded, which survives the reboot. See correction #14 in docs/05.
